# Process / CLI I/O

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. What CLI tools and containerized services actually need day-to-day (argument parsing, stdin, environment config, exit codes). Prioritized because the long-term project direction favors CLI/microservice use cases. `console.log`/`.error` already write to stdout/stderr respectively — see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md) — the gaps below are everything *else* a CLI program needs.

**Coverage**: 32/32 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 13/32 (~41%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Command-line arguments (`process.argv`) | ✅ | • Mirrors C's `argv` directly (`argv[0]` is the binary's own path), not Node's two-prefix convention — see [ADR-00002](../adr/ADR-00002.md)<br>• An out-of-range `process.argv[i]` read yields `""` (falsy), not Node's `undefined` and not the general array bounds throw ([ADR-00425](../adr/ADR-00425.md)) | |
| Environment variables (`process.env.KEY` / `process.env["KEY"]`) | ✅ | | • Both dot and bracket notation; returns a possibly-null string (same convention as `.find()`), so `process.env.X ?? "default"` works |
| Exit codes (`process.exit(code)`) | ✅ | | • Calls C `exit()`; never returns, code after it is correctly unreachable |
| Reading stdin (sync line read) | ✅ | | • `process.readLineSync()` — one line via POSIX `getline()` (handles arbitrarily long lines), stripped of its trailing `\n`/`\r\n`. Returns `null` at EOF (same possibly-null convention as `process.env`). See [ADR-00024](../adr/ADR-00024.md). |
| Simple synchronous file read/write (`fs.readFileSync`/`writeFileSync`-style) | ✅ | | • See [FILE-SYSTEM.md](FILE-SYSTEM.md) |
| `process.execFileSync(file, args?)` | ✅ | • No options object (no `cwd`/`env`/`timeout`/`stdio` overrides yet)<br>• stderr is inherited (visible on the terminal live), not captured | • Node's `child_process.execFileSync`, not `execSync`: `fork()`+`execvp()`s `file` directly with no shell involved, so shell metacharacters in `args` are never interpreted<br>• Returns captured stdout as a string; throws a catchable `Error` on a non-zero exit status or a signal death. See [ADR-00025](../adr/ADR-00025.md). |
| `process.cwd()` | ✅ | | • Current working directory, via POSIX `getcwd(NULL, 0)` (auto-sizing). See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md). |
| `process.chdir(path)` | ✅ | | • Changes the current working directory via POSIX `chdir()`. Throws a catchable `Error` (same "`<opDesc>` '`<path>`': `<strerror>`" shape `fs.*`'s failures already use) if the path doesn't exist or isn't a directory. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md). |
| `process.pid` | ✅ | | • The current process ID, via POSIX `getpid()`. A property read, not a call, matching `process.argv`. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md). |
| `process.platform` | ✅ | | • A pure compile-time constant (`"darwin"`/`"linux"`/`"win32"`/...) baked in from the Go compiler's own `runtime.GOOS` — no runtime code at all, since this compiler doesn't cross-compile. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md). |
| `process.arch` | ✅ | | • A compile-time constant (`"arm64"`/`"x64"`/...) from the Go compiler's `runtime.GOARCH`, exactly like `process.platform` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md)) |
| `process.execPath` | ✅ | | • The absolute, symlink-resolved path of the running executable — the compiled program is itself the binary (no separate runtime), resolved via `_NSGetExecutablePath`+`realpath` (macOS) / `/proc/self/exe` (Linux), so it's always absolute like Node's, not a raw `argv[0]` ([ADR-00395](../adr/ADR-00395.md)) |
| `process.emitWarning(message, type?)` | ✅ | • No options-object form (`{ code, detail }`) and no first-warning `--trace-warnings` hint line | • Writes `(node:<pid>) <type>: <message>` to stderr, `type` defaulting to `"Warning"`, and (like Node's always-on default printer) additionally invokes any `process.on('warning', …)` listener with the warning as an `Error` ([ADR-00395](../adr/ADR-00395.md)/[ADR-00401](../adr/ADR-00401.md)) |
| `process.kill(pid, signal?)` | ✅ | | • Sends `signal` (defaults to `15`/`SIGTERM`, matching real Node) to `pid` via POSIX `kill()`. Throws a catchable `Error` if the target process doesn't exist or the signal can't be sent; signal `0` is the standard POSIX "does this process exist" check and never actually delivers a signal. See [ADR-00026](../adr/ADR-00026.md). |
| `process.stdout.write(s)` / `process.stderr.write(s)` (raw write, no auto-newline) | ✅ | • Text-only (byte-string, not binary-safe past an embedded null — same scope narrowing `console.log`'s own string formatting already has)<br>• Beyond `.write`, `.isTTY` (a real `isatty(fd)` probe on all three stdio handles — [ADR-00424](../adr/ADR-00424.md)), and `.columns`/`.rows` (a live `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` read — [ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)), `process.stdout`/`stderr` expose no other stream surface (no `'drain'`) | • Unlike `console.log`/`.error` (always a trailing newline), a plain write of exactly `s` with nothing appended — useful for a progress indicator or assembling one line from several pieces<br>• `stdout` goes through buffered `printf` (matching `console.log`'s own fd=1 convention, so output ordering against `console.log` calls elsewhere in the same program stays correct); `stderr` goes through unbuffered `dprintf` (matching `console.error`'s own fd=2 convention) |
| `process.stdout.columns` / `.rows` (terminal size) | ✅ | • Off a non-TTY (piped/redirected) returns an 80x24 fallback rather than Node's `undefined` — this compiler has no clean undefined-number ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)) | • A live `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` read on each access (never cached, matching Node); pair with `process.on('SIGWINCH')` to repaint on resize<br>• Available on both `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` |
| `process.stdin.setRawMode(enabled)` (raw terminal input) | ✅ | • A no-op when fd 0 is not a terminal (`tcgetattr` fails) — guard on `process.stdin.isTTY` first, as every TUI does<br>• Raw mode disables signal generation (`ISIG`), so Ctrl-C stops delivering `SIGINT` and arrives as the raw byte `3` for the program to handle — matching Node/libuv `UV_TTY_MODE_RAW` exactly<br>• Auto-restore on a crash/uncaught exception is the application's responsibility (same footgun as Node); `setRawMode(false)` restores the state captured on the first enable | • Routes through an embedded C shim compiled against the platform's own `<termios.h>`, so the glibc/Darwin `struct termios` layout difference is sidestepped by construction ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md))<br>• Pair with `process.stdin.on('data')` (event-driven, the Node-idiomatic raw loop) or with `klain:tty` `readByte`/`readKey` (synchronous) |
| `klain:tty` `readByte()` / `readKey()` (synchronous raw reads) | ✅ | • Bespoke, non-Node surface under the explicit `klain:` specifier — Node has no synchronous single-key read (it uses `process.stdin.on('data')` events)<br>• Blocking reads on fd 0; do not mix with `process.stdin.on('data')` in the same run, which puts fd 0 in non-blocking mode (a synchronous read would then see EOF-on-EAGAIN) | • `readByte()` returns one byte (or -1 at EOF); `readKey()` returns one `read()`'s whole burst as a string, so an escape sequence like an arrow key (ESC `[` A) is a single key ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)) |
| Writing `process.env` (`process.env.KEY = val` / `process.env["KEY"] = val`) | ✅ | • Compound assignment (`process.env.X += …`) is a clean rejection | • `setenv(key, String(val), overwrite)` ([ADR-00333](../adr/ADR-00333.md)); a written variable is inherited by child processes<br>• `delete process.env.KEY` unsets the variable for real ([ADR-00487](../adr/ADR-00487.md)) |
| `process.on('SIGINT'/'SIGTERM'/'SIGWINCH', handler)` (signal handlers) | ✅ | • The handler runs from ordinary control flow at the top of the event loop's own iteration, never from real async signal context<br>• Event name must be a compile-time string literal, exactly `'SIGINT'`/`'SIGTERM'`/`'SIGWINCH'` (dynamic event names are a clean compile error, matching `Object.hasOwn`'s dynamic-key rejection)<br>• Handler must be a zero-argument `() => void` closure, same shape `setTimeout`'s own callback requires<br>• One handler slot per signal — registering the same signal twice overwrites the previous handler<br>• Only fires while a `http.listen`-driven or timer-driven event loop is actively iterating; a plain synchronous script with neither has no loop to check from | • Lets a running program (e.g. an `http.listen` server) intercept a signal and shut down gracefully instead of dying immediately. See [TDD-00019](../tdd/TDD-00019.md)/[ADR-00079](../adr/ADR-00079.md), [HTTP-SERVER.md](HTTP-SERVER.md).<br>• `'SIGWINCH'` (terminal resize) lets a TUI re-read `process.stdout.columns`/`.rows` and repaint on a window resize ([ADR-00518](../adr/ADR-00518.md)) |
| `process.on('exit'/'uncaughtException'/'warning', ...)` + `process.exitCode` | ✅ | • `'uncaughtException'` runs the listener (suppressing the default `Uncaught:` print) but the process still exits (code 1) — the setjmp/longjmp exception model has already unwound to the top-level catch-all, so it can't resume execution like Node does<br>• `'warning'` fires (with the warning as an `Error`) when `process.emitWarning` is called; the stderr print still happens too<br>• No `'unhandledRejection'` yet (needs rejected-promise tracking)<br>• One listener slot per event, arrow-literal only | • `'exit'` fires at normal end and from `process.exit()`, receiving the exit code; `process.exitCode = N` sets the deferred code a bare program returns; `process.exit()` with no argument uses it ([ADR-00334](../adr/ADR-00334.md)/[ADR-00401](../adr/ADR-00401.md)) |
| `process.hrtime()` / `process.hrtime.bigint()` | ✅ | • `hrtime()` takes no argument — the legacy diff-from-a-previous-reading form isn't supported (use `.bigint()` and subtract) | • `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` via the same layer as `performance.now()` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md)); `hrtime()` → a `[seconds, nanoseconds]` tuple, `.bigint()` → total-nanoseconds bigint |
| `process.getuid()` / `geteuid()` / `getgid()` / `getegid()` | ✅ | | • Direct POSIX credential reads returning a `number` — present unconditionally (this compiler is POSIX-only), matching Node-on-POSIX ([ADR-00428](../adr/ADR-00428.md)) |
| `process.memoryUsage()` | ✅ | • Only `rss` carries a real value; `heapTotal`/`heapUsed`/`external`/`arrayBuffers` report 0 — there is no managed V8 heap to measure in a native build, so they are returned zeroed rather than fabricated<br>• `rss` reports *peak* resident set (`ru_maxrss`), not the instantaneous value Node returns | • `rss` is the process's peak resident set size, read from `getrusage(2)`'s `ru_maxrss` (bytes on macOS, kilobytes scaled on Linux) ([ADR-00507](../adr/ADR-00507.md)) |
| `process.nextTick(fn)` | ✅ | • Shares the one microtask FIFO with Promise reactions rather than draining strictly before them (Node keeps a separate nextTick queue ahead of promises); zero-argument `() => void` callback only | • Enqueued on the existing microtask queue ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md)) |
| `process.version` / `process.versions` | ✅ | • `versions` reports only honest values — `node`/`v8` (the pinned Node compatibility baseline, v22.11.0) and `klain` (this compiler's version); it deliberately omits bundled-lib keys this compiler doesn't ship (`uv`/`undici`/`icu`/…) rather than fabricate them<br>• The real linked-library versions we *can* report truthfully (`openssl` under the OpenSSL backend, `zlib` when linked) are a follow-on — they need a runtime lib query + backend-aware linking<br>• `node`/`v8` track the compatibility *ceiling* (the pinned test-corpus release); a `--node-compat` floor is deferred ([TDD-00136](../tdd/TDD-00136.md)) | • `process.version` = `"v22.11.0"`; `process.versions` is a real object (`JSON.stringify`/field access/`Object.keys` all work), matching Node v22.11.0's `node`/`v8` verbatim ([ADR-00396](../adr/ADR-00396.md)) |
| `process.uptime()` | ✅ | | • Seconds (a `double`) since process start, captured once at `main` entry via `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` ([ADR-00332](../adr/ADR-00332.md)) |
| `process.stdin` (streamed reads, not just `readLineSync()`) | ✅ | • `'data'` delivers each read chunk as a UTF-8 string, not a `Buffer` — no `setEncoding`, no binary mode<br>• Flowing mode only (attaching `'data'` starts it) — no `.pause()`/`.resume()`/`.read()`/`'readable'`<br>• One listener per event, arrow/function-expression literal only; callbacks fire synchronously from the dispatch, not via a microtask | • `process.stdin.on('data'/'end')` over a non-blocking fd 0 folded into the same `select()` loop as `readline`/`child_process` ([ADR-00339](../adr/ADR-00339.md)); `'data'` per read chunk, `'end'` once on EOF. Distinct from the blocking `process.readLineSync()` and the line-oriented `readline` module above |
| `readline` module (`createInterface`, `'line'`/`'close'` events, `question()`, `close()`) | ✅ | • The listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through a microtask queue (same as `child_process`)<br>• One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only; no line history/editing, no `SIGINT`/`'pause'`/`'resume'`, no completer<br>• The `createInterface` options object is accepted but ignored — input is always stdin, output always stdout; one active interface at a time | • Non-blocking stdin (fd 0) folded into the same `select()` loop as `child_process` ([ADR-00323](../adr/ADR-00323.md)); emits one `'line'` per newline (CR stripped), flushes an unterminated final line on EOF then fires `'close'`. Distinct from the blocking `process.readLineSync()` above |
| `child_process.spawn()` / `.exec()` / `.execFile()` (async, event-driven) | ✅ | • The listener callbacks fire synchronously from the event loop's dispatch, not deferred through the microtask queue (`process.nextTick`, which does not exist yet — see the row above)<br>• One listener per event, an arrow/function-expression literal only (the same posture as `Worker`); no `removeListener`<br>• spawn's options support `{ cwd, shell, stdio: 'pipe' }` ([ADR-00433](../adr/ADR-00433.md)) — `cwd` is real (child chdir), `shell` is accepted but **ignored** (commands always exec directly, never via a shell), and `env`/`detached`/stdio arrays are clean rejections; exec/execFile still take no options. `'close'`/`'exit'` receive the exit `code` only (a signal death is folded to `128+signal`, no separate `signal` argument)<br>• Handles and their buffered output are never freed (`-mm=manual`) | • fork()+execvp() with three pipes; the two read ends are non-blocking and fold into the same `select()` event loop as Worker/channel pipes ([ADR-00322](../adr/ADR-00322.md))<br>• `spawn` streams (`child.stdout`/`stderr` `'data'`/`'end'`, `child.on('close'/'exit')`, `child.stdin.write`/`.end`, `child.pid`, `child.kill`); `exec` runs via `/bin/sh -c` and `execFile` execvp's directly, both buffering into a single `(err, stdout, stderr)` callback |
| `child_process.fork()` (self-fork + IPC channel) | ✅ | • Self-fork only: the path must be `__filename` or `process.argv[1]` (forking a *different* module would need a second compiled program — clean rejection); the options object must be an empty `{}`<br>• Messages are strings (`send(obj)` is a clean rejection); one `'message'` listener per side<br>• Bare `process.send` reads as a *boolean* forked-ness probe, not Node's function-or-undefined — `assert.strictEqual(process.send, undefined)`-style tests type-mismatch cleanly<br>• `process.argv[i]` out-of-range reads yield `""` (falsy) rather than Node's `undefined` — the `argv[2] === 'child'` / `if (!argv[2])` idioms behave; a strict compare against `undefined` doesn't | • Node's own mechanism ([TDD-00141](../tdd/TDD-00141.md)/[ADR-00425](../adr/ADR-00425.md)): socketpair + re-exec of the current binary with `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` set; child argv layout `[exe, modulePath, ...args]` so extra args land at `argv[2]`; NDJSON string frames (embedded C, linked only when used)<br>• Parent: `child.send(str)→bool`, `child.on('message'/'exit'/'close')`, `child.disconnect()`, inherited stdio; child: `process.send(str)→bool` (false unforked), `process.on('message')` (holds the event loop open while connected), `process.disconnect()`; `mustCall`-wrapped listeners contextually typed |
| `child_process.spawnSync()` / `.execSync()` / `.execFileSync()` (blocking) | ✅ | • Options object supports `{ cwd, encoding: 'utf8' }` only (no `env`/`timeout`/`input`/`shell`/`stdio` — clean rejections); results are strings (the `encoding: 'utf8'` shape), not Buffers<br>• `spawnSync`'s result carries `status`/`stdout`/`stderr`/`pid` only — no `signal`/`error`/`output` fields (a signal death folds into `status` as `128+signal`)<br>• `execSync`/`execFileSync` return stdout but do **not** throw on a non-zero exit status (Node throws) — use `spawnSync().status` where the exit code matters | • One embedded C core ([ADR-00411](../adr/ADR-00411.md)): fork + execvp with both stdio pipes poll-multiplexed to completion (no deadlock when a child fills stderr while stdout drains), then a blocking waitpid; `execSync` runs via `/bin/sh -c`<br>• Distinct from the bespoke `process.execFileSync` above (which throws on failure and inherits stderr) |
